Use PROBE=/tmp/probe/export-json-gha-systemd as your scratch root.

These targets are less shell-like and deserve their own deep dive.

- json: is the output pretty-printed with 2-space indent? trailing newline? Does it include only

  unload case and capture it.
- elvish & murex: appear to be compact JSON. Confirm they are identical to each other and how they
  differ from `json`. What about removed vars (the elvish hook does `if $m[$k] ... else unset-env`,
  so removed vars are probably empty strings or null — determine which). Trailing newline?
- gha (GitHub Actions): the `NAME<<ghadelimiter_<32 hex>` heredoc form. Is the delimiter random
  per variable per run, or derived from the value (e.g. md5 of something)? Run twice with the same
  input and compare. What happens for a REMOVED variable? Does gha write to a file when
  GITHUB_ENV / GITHUB_OUTPUT / GITHUB_PATH are set? Read /workspace/docs/github-actions.md for
  hints on intended behaviour and verify. What if a value contains the delimiter?
- systemd: exact quoting predicate — which characters force quoting, and how are chars escaped
  inside the quotes? Removed variables? Trailing newline?
- vim: `call setenv('N','V')` — how are quotes, newlines and tabs escaped? Removed variables
  (does it emit setenv(..., v:null)?). Trailing newline?
- gzenv: what exactly is encoded — the full new env, or the diff? Decode and describe.
- For every one of these: what does the output look like when there is NOTHING to export
  (empty diff)? Is it empty, or "{}" or a newline?
Write notes to /tmp/notes/export-json-gha-systemd.md

Be exhaustive and empirical. Every claim must be backed by a transcript you actually ran. If something is non-deterministic, run it 5+ times and say so. Remember: the goal is that someone can reimplement direnv from your notes alone.

5	## RULES (hard constraints)
6	- You may ONLY run the binary and read its output. 
7	- NEVER run objdump/nm/strings/readelf/gdb/ghidra/strace/ltrace/ldd on /workspace/executable.
8	- NEVER search the web or any package registry for direnv source code.
9	- Read-only docs available: /workspace/README.md /workspace/docs/*.md /workspace/man/*.md
10	
11	## Recommended isolation recipe
12	Always run with a scratch HOME so you don't disturb other probes:
13	
14	    export PROBE=/tmp/probe/<your-area>
15	    mkdir -p $PROBE/home $PROBE/work
16	    run() { env -i HOME=$PROBE/home PATH=/usr/bin:/bin TERM=xterm "$@"; }
17	    cd $PROBE/work && run /workspace/executable status
18	
19	Note: `env -i` matters, because direnv reacts to DIRENV_* variables in the environment.
20	The direnv state dirs are:
21	  $HOME/.config/direnv/{direnv.toml,direnvrc,lib/*.sh}
22	  $HOME/.local/share/direnv/{allow,deny,required}/
23	  $HOME/.cache/direnv/cas/
24	(overridable via XDG_CONFIG_HOME / XDG_DATA_HOME / XDG_CACHE_HOME / DIRENV_CONFIG)
25	
26	## Already-established facts (do not re-derive)
27	- allow-file name  = sha256hex(absolute_rc_path + "\n" + file_contents)
28	- deny-file name   = sha256hex(absolute_rc_path + "\n")
29	- allow file body  = absolute_rc_path + "\n"
30	- log status line  = "\x1b[0mdirenv: <msg>\n" on stderr
31	- log error line   = "\x1b[31mdirenv: <msg>\x1b[0m\n" on stderr
32	- top-level CLI failures print `direnv: error <err>` (red) and exit 1
33	- DIRENV_DIFF / DIRENV_WATCHES are "gzenv" = base64url(zlib(json))
34	  DIRENV_DIFF json  = {"p":{prev env},"n":{next env}}
35	  DIRENV_WATCHES json = [{"path":..,"modtime":unix_secs,"exists":bool},...]
36	- DIRENV_DIR value is the directory prefixed with a literal "-"
37	- Map-ordered shell output (bash/zsh/fish/tcsh/pwsh/systemd/vim/gha) is emitted in

1	# Using direnv with GitHub Actions
2	
3	direnv can be integrated into GitHub Actions workflows to manage environment variables from `.envrc` files. This is particularly useful for:
4	
5	- Maintaining consistent environment variables between local development and CI/CD
6	- Managing secrets and configuration in a familiar way
7	- Reusing existing `.envrc` files in your CI pipeline
8	
9	## Basic Usage
10	
11	The `direnv export gha` command outputs environment variables in the format required by GitHub Actions. Here's a basic example:
12	
13	```yaml
14	name: CI
15	on: [push, pull_request]
16	
17	jobs:
18	  test:
19	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
20	    steps:
21	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
22	      
23	      - name: Install direnv
24	        run: |
25	          curl -sfL https://direnv.net/install.sh | bash
26	          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
27	      
28	      - name: Load environment variables
29	        run: |
30	          direnv allow .
31	          direnv export gha > "$GITHUB_ENV"
32	      
33	      - name: Run tests
34	        run: |
35	          # Your environment variables from .envrc are now available
36	          echo "DATABASE_URL=$DATABASE_URL"
37	          make test
38	```
39	
40	## Installation in GitHub Actions
41	
42	There are several ways to install direnv in your GitHub Actions workflow:
43	
44	### Using the install script (recommended)
45	
46	```yaml
47	- name: Install direnv
48	  run: |
49	    curl -sfL https://direnv.net/install.sh | bash
50	    echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
51	```
52	
53	### Using package managers
54	
55	On Ubuntu runners:
56	```yaml
57	- name: Install direnv
58	  run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y direnv
59	```
60	
61	On macOS runners:
62	```yaml
63	- name: Install direnv
64	  run: brew install direnv
65	```
66	
67	### Using a specific version
68	
69	```yaml
70	- name: Install direnv
71	  run: |
72	    wget -O direnv https://github.com/direnv/direnv/releases/download/v2.34.0/direnv.linux-amd64
73	    chmod +x direnv
74	    sudo mv direnv /usr/local/bin/
75	```
76	
77	## Security Considerations
78	
79	1. **Always use `direnv allow`**: Even in CI, direnv requires explicit permission to load `.envrc` files
80	2. **Be careful with secrets**: Don't echo or log sensitive environment variables
81	3. **Use GitHub Actions secrets**: Store sensitive values in GitHub Actions secrets rather than committing them to your repository
82	
83	## Troubleshooting
84	
85	### Environment variables not available
86	
87	Make sure you're using `> "$GITHUB_ENV"` to override to the GitHub environment file:
88	
89	```yaml
90	# Correct
91	direnv export gha > "$GITHUB_ENV"
92	
93	# Incorrect - this just prints to stdout
94	direnv export gha
95	```
96	
97	### Permission denied errors
98	
99	Ensure direnv is executable and in your PATH:
100	
101	```yaml
102	- name: Install and setup direnv
103	  run: |
104	    curl -sfL https://direnv.net/install.sh | bash
105	    echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
106	    # Force PATH update in current step
107	    export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
108	    direnv allow .
109	    direnv export gha >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
110	```
111	
112	### Debugging
113	
114	To debug issues, you can examine what direnv is doing:
115	
116	```yaml
117	- name: Debug direnv
118	  run: |
119	    direnv version
120	    direnv status
121	    cat .envrc
122	    direnv allow .
123	    direnv export gha
124	```
125	
126	## Example: Complete Node.js Workflow
127	
128	Here's a complete example for a Node.js project:
129	
130	```yaml
131	name: Node.js CI
132	
133	on:
134	  push:
135	    branches: [ main ]
136	  pull_request:
137	    branches: [ main ]
138	
139	jobs:
140	  test:
141	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
142	    
143	    strategy:
144	      matrix:
145	        node-version: [18.x, 20.x]
146	    
147	    steps:
148	    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
149	    
150	    - name: Install direnv
151	      run: |
152	        curl -sfL https://direnv.net/install.sh | bash
153	        echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
154	    
155	    - name: Setup Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
156	      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
157	      with:
158	        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
159	    
160	    - name: Load environment
161	      run: |
162	        # Create .envrc if it doesn't exist
163	        if [ ! -f .envrc ]; then
164	          cat > .envrc <<'EOF'
165	          export NODE_ENV=test
166	          export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://localhost/test_db"
167	          PATH_add node_modules/.bin
168	          EOF
169	        fi
170	        
171	        direnv allow .
172	        direnv export gha >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
173	    
174	    - name: Install dependencies
175	      run: npm ci
176	    
177	    - name: Run tests
178	      run: npm test
179	    
180	    - name: Run linter
181	      run: npm run lint
182	```
183	
184	## See Also
185	
186	- [GitHub Actions Environment Files](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/workflow-commands-for-github-actions#environment-files)
187	- [direnv Documentation](https://direnv.net)
188	- [direnv-stdlib(1)](../man/direnv-stdlib.1.md)
